Please solve this issue: Finance writes off invoices that will never be paid. Add `write_off(invoice, at, reason)` to `ledgerly/adjustments.py`: it marks an issued invoice as `"void"` and returns a dict with the keys `invoice_id`, `amount` (the invoice total) and `reason`. Only issued invoices can be written off.

## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0002] Use to_money and ZERO from money module: Convert line amounts with ledgerly.money.to_money and accumulate Decimal sums starting from ledgerly.money.ZERO, as done in invoice_total and line_total in ledgerly/invoice.py.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Signal domain failures by raising BillingError(code, detail) from ledgerly.errors with stable snake_case codes such as "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity" and "negative_amount", matching the codes used in ledgerly.invoice.issue_invoice.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary values with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0007] Money operations need idempotency_key support: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`; check `ledgerly.audit.events()` for a matching key first and return the original result without reapplying, and include the key in the audit entry (INC-204).
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0009] Audit entries store amounts as float: When writing audit entries, pass the amount as `float(amount)`; the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

## Code review of your previous attempt
Your previous attempt at this issue was reviewed and not accepted. The repository still contains that attempt. Address every comment below:
- [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must write an audit entry with ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...), where <entity> is the payment or invoice the money moves against (payment_id=... or invoice_id=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
- [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
- [team convention] Money in ledgerly is Decimal end-to-end and always has exactly two decimal places. Never convert amounts to float.
